newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle seen steady-lower, market pauses.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle seen steady-lower, market pauses.

text.p: CME live cattle were seen opening steady to 0.10 cent per lb lower as the market drifts down in the absence of fed cattle trade, traders said.
Feeder cattle futures were called to open steady to 0.10 higher on gains in the CME feeder cattle index and good demand in cash markets, sources said.
"Normally after you put money on the (fed cattle) cash market, traders step back from the futures market," one livestock analyst said.
However, firm wholesale beef prices and expectations for higher cash cattle next week were seen underpinning prices.
"Showlists are sold out, feedlots are current, beef movement is good--there's no reason to get short," said Dale Benson, livestock analyst with Dean Witter in Chicago.
Those supportive fundamental factors have some bulls predicting that cash cattle will trade $1.00 higher at $72.00 cwt next week.
Weakness in early live cattle trade was seen stemming from Wednesday's modest sell-off at the close as well as profit taking before the weekend, traders and analysts said.
Feeder cattle futures were seen posting modest gains early because demand for feeder cattle in cash markets was said to be solid.
A $0.05 jump to $62.11 cwt in the latest CME feeder cattle index was also viewed as supportive, traders and analysts said.
